## Q1
1.
```{r}
#simulations
n <- 10000

x1 <- runif(n, min = 1, max = 3)
#function
y1 <- x1^2
(3 - 1) * mean(y1) #MC estimate
(3 - 1) * sd(y1) / sqrt(n) #SE
27/3 - 1/3 #exact 
```
```{r}
x2 <- runif(n, min = 1, max = pi)
#function
y2 <- exp(x2)
(pi - 1) * mean(y2) #MC estimate
(pi - 1) * sd(y2) / sqrt(n) #SE
exp(pi) - exp(1) #exact
```
```{r}
#exponential rand nums
x3 <- rexp(n, rate = 1)

#importance sampling
#(adjust function using prob density)
y3 <- exp(x3 - x3^3)
mean(y3) #MC estimate
sd(y3) / sqrt(n) #SE
```
```{r}
x4 <- runif(n, min = 0, max = 1)
#function
y4 <- (1 / sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(-x4^2 / 2)
mean(y4) #MC estimaet
sd(y4) / sqrt(n) #SE 
```

Monte Carlo integration gives estimates that should be near the exact values but the estimates aren't identical because they are from randomly generated samples.

3.
```{r}
#generate Gaussian quadrature nodes and weights from uniform distrib
gq1 <- statmod::gauss.quad.prob(n = 20, dist = "uniform")

(3 - 1) * sum(gq1$weights * (1 + 2*gq1$nodes)^2) #integral (square nodes X²)
27/3 - 1/3 #exact 

gq2 <- statmod::gauss.quad.prob(n = 20, dist = "uniform") #2nd integral

(pi - 1) * sum(gq2$weights * exp(1 +(pi -1)*gq2$nodes)) #integral
exp(pi) - exp(1) #exact
```

## Q2
1.
```{r}
# pdf of Kumaraswamy
dkumaraswamy <- function(x, a, b) {
  result <- a* b * x^(a - 1)* (1 - x^a)^(b - 1)
  return(result)
}

dkumaraswamy(x =c(0.3, 0.6, 0.9), a = 1, b = 2)
```

2.
```{r}
#default arguments
dkumaraswamy2 <- function(x, a = 1, b = 1) {
  #check if a and b valid
  if (a <= 0 || b <= 0) {
    stop("a and b must be greater than zero")}

  # if both are 1 it has unif distrib
  if (a == 1 & b == 1) {
    return(dunif(x))}
  
  result <- a* b * x^(a - 1)* (1 - x^a)^(b - 1)
  return(result)
}
dkumaraswamy2(x = c(0.3, 0.6, 0.9))
dunif(x = c(0.3, 0.6, 0.9))
```

3.
```{r}
curve(dkumaraswamy2(x), ylim = c(0, 3), col = "black")
curve(dkumaraswamy2(x, a = 0.5, b = 0.5), ylim = c(0, 3), col = "red", add =TRUE)
curve(dkumaraswamy2(x, a = 2, b = 5), ylim = c(0, 3), col = "blue", add =TRUE)
```

4.
```{r}
rkumaraswamy <- function(a, b, n) {
  u <- runif(n) #get n unif nums
  #inverse CDF
  x <- (1 -(1 - u)^(1/b))^(1/a)
  return(x)
}

samples <- rkumaraswamy(a =2, b =5, n =10000)
head(samples)
```

```{r}
curve(dkumaraswamy2(x), ylim = c(0, 3), col = "black")
curve(dkumaraswamy2(x, a = 0.5, b = 0.5), ylim = c(0, 3), col = "red", add =TRUE)
curve(dkumaraswamy2(x, a = 2, b = 5), ylim = c(0, 3), col = "blue", add =TRUE)

lines(density(samples,kernel = "epanechnikov"),
      col = "green", lwd = 2, lty = 3) #R auto sets bw
```

## Q3
```{r}
#Marsaglia params
a <- 69069
b <- 1
M <- 2^32

n <- 10000
#empty vector
x <- numeric(n)

x[1] <- 2345 #initial seed

#generate sequence
for (i in 2:n) {
  x[i] <- (a * x[i-1] + b) %% M #Marsaglia formula
}
#change to unif rand nums
u <- x / M

U <- data.frame(u1 = u[1:(n-2)],
                u2 = u[2:(n-1)],
                u3 = u[3:n])

#special ordering ui−1 < ui+1 < ui
event <- U$u1 < U$u3 & U$u3 < U$u2

#percentage event occurs (should be 1/6)
(sum(event) / length(event)) * 100
```

## Q4
1. & 2.
```{r}
set.seed(23453144)

box_muller <- function(numpairs) {
  #unif rand nums
  u1 <- runif(numpairs)
  u2 <- runif(numpairs)
  
  theta <- 2*pi * u1
  R <- sqrt(2 * -log(u2))

  #make standard norm variables
  x1 <- R * cos(theta)
  x2 <- R * sin(theta)

  #return both vectors 
  return(c(x1, x2))}

z <- box_muller(5000)
length(z)
```

3.
```{r}
part3 <- sqrt(3) * z + 10 #variance = 3 we need s.d

mean(part3)
sd(part3)
var(part3)
```

4.

